THE OPERATOR

About

I'm Andrew Campbell. I've spent fifteen years building go-to-market systems — product marketing, revenue architecture, pipeline design — across EdTech, enterprise automation, data technology, fintech, and AI.

I have a PhD in chemistry, which is mostly relevant because of how it makes me work: hypothesis, instrument, measure, iterate. Most go-to-market problems aren't strategy problems. They're measurement problems wearing a strategy costume.

For most of my career I was the person inside the company who could see what was broken. Now I do that from outside, and I bring the tools to fix it.

WHY THE NAME

Iron is soft. Carbon is brittle. Together they're steel.

An alloy is what you get when two elements fuse into something neither could be alone.

Most GTM help arrives as one element or the other. The strategist diagnoses and departs. The software solves a narrow problem and leaves implementation to you.

I do both halves. That's the whole idea.

Yes, the chemistry background is why the metaphor is there. No, it isn't an accident.

METHOD

How I work

  • Integration over replacement.

    Most companies don't need a new stack. They need the one they're already paying for to actually work together.

  • Diagnose before building.

    Agencies run their playbook regardless of fit. The playbook comes second.

  • Signal over noise.

    Activity metrics are comfortable and mostly useless. The work is finding the small number of behaviors that actually predict revenue, then instrumenting for those.

  • Build it rather than recommend it.

    If something can be built inside the engagement, it gets built.

CLARIFICATIONS

Frequently asked questions

Q-01How is this different from an agency?

Agencies run their playbook regardless of whether it fits. Diagnosis comes first here, and only what your situation needs gets built.

Q-02How is this different from a fractional CMO?

Most fractional CMOs direct work. I do the work — inside your HubSpot, your n8n, your data.

Q-03We already have tools. Do we have to switch?

Almost never. Integration over replacement. Half the job is making what you already pay for work together.

Q-04How technical does this get?

As technical as needed. CRM architecture, workflow automation, SQL-level data cleanup, custom internal tools, API and MCP integrations.

Q-05Where are you based?

Austin, Texas. Work is remote.
